newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha to quit after election loss.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha to quit after election loss.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha, confronted with a Socialist victory in general elections, said on Wednesday he intended to resign once a leftist government came to power.

"Definitely. There is no doubt of that. I never had the smallest doubt in that respect," Berisha told a news conference in English when asked repeatedly whether he intended to quit if a leftist government was formed.
Berisha said he intended to step down as soon as legal procedures allowed.

"I have some crucial duties and responsibilities that I have to fulfil," he said. "One thing is sure. I am interested in seeing it completed as soon as possible, but it does not depend on me. What depends on me I will try to accelerate."

Berisha had pledged during the campaign to step down if his Democratic Party, in power since 1992, was beaten into opposition. He had already conceded defeat and partial returns from last Sunday's voting put the Socialists in the lead.

Under Albania's post-Communist laws, Berisha is elected by parliament and must submit any resignation to the assembly. The 155-seat parliament can only be convened after the completion on Sunday of run-offs in districts where no candidate won the required 50 percent in of the vote in the first round.
Berisha also said he had asked Socialist Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to propose an interior minister to replace Belul Celo, who he said had left the country.
"There is no interior minister and there is no commander of operations," he said.
He said that under a March agreement to set up a multi-party government and stage last Sunday's election the appointee had to be from his Democratic Party.
A confrontation had erupted earlier on Wednesday between the two men over control of the interior ministry, which is responsible for the armed forces.
Berisha said he had ordered police and elite troops to erect roadblocks on approach roads to Tirana to prevent an influx of Socialist supporters into the capital.
Fino accused Berisha of interfering by trying to appoint another of his loyalists even though Celo was still in office.
